svg.title: Is a dismissal fair?
svg.desc: A dismissal is automatically unfair if the reason is, for example, pregnancy, joining a union or a protected strike, discrimination, or using your labour rights. Otherwise it is fair only if it has both a fair reason, which is your conduct, your capacity or the employer's operational requirements, and a fair procedure, meaning you were told the problem and given a fair chance to answer first. Missing either one makes it unfair.
svg.text: The employer has to prove it was fair. It needs both of these:
Capacity: poor work or long illness
Usually after warnings, help or consultation
You're told what the problem is
You get a fair chance to answer,
Pregnancy. Joining a union or a protected strike. Discrimination.
Using your labour rights. Reporting wrongdoing (a protected disclosure).
Source: Labour Relations Act sections 185 to 192; CCMA info sheet. Legal information, not legal advice.
